title: Eval steering controller for staged A/B reversion
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build an Eval Steering Controller that automatically governs staged A/B rollouts by continuously scoring quality delta on a designated probe set and driving automated traffic reversion when defined safety and utility thresholds are breached. This work closes the gap between offline eval signals and live rollback actions while minimizing false positives and preserving business throughput.
motivation: We have frequent manual interventions during staged A/B experiments because QA signals surface late or are noisy. Engineering time is spent triaging ambiguous regressions; customers sometimes see degraded quality during prolonged exposures. The controller should provide explainable, statistically-sound reversion decisions, with a low false revert rate and clear audit trail.
goals: Implement online eval scoring pipeline that computes per-cohort deltas for primary quality metrics within 5-minute windows
Define a decision engine using Bayesian sequential testing to trigger automated reversion with configurable minimum effect size and confidence
Integrate controller with rollout plane to adjust traffic fractions and initiate safe reversion paths (full revert, stepback by X%, or quarantine)
Expose per-rollout provenance and reasoning in Console and audit logs for post-mortem and compliance
non_goals: Replacing human review for high-sensitivity enterprise audits; humans remain approvers for security-sensitive deploys
Reworking model training or dataset curation — this is an inference-side control layer only
acceptance_criteria: Controller triggers automated revert in staging A/B when synthetic probe set shows a >5% drop in instruction-following score with posterior probability > 98%
False revert rate on historical test harness < 1% across 6 months of recorded rollouts
Console shows causal provenance for each automated action including metric deltas, confidence interval, and contributing probe examples
Controller respects tiered opt-outs: 'manual-only' for enterprise customers with private deployments
End-to-end latency from metric compute to traffic change < 2 minutes in normal operation
tech_design: Data plane: lightweight probe runner that executes a curated probe set per-route + per-cohort; probes are small (~200 examples) and labeled by expected behavior

Aggregation: time-windowed aggregator (5m, 15m, 1h) that computes weighted deltas for metrics: instruction-following accuracy, hallucination rate (fact-check probe failures), token KL divergence vs control, and latency percentile regression
Decision engine: Bayesian sequential test (beta-binomial for binary probes, Gaussian for continuous metrics) with configurable minimum effect size and prior tuned from historical rollout data

Safety heuristics: multi-metric veto (e.g., if any of hallucination rate or safety-critical checks worsen beyond threshold, immediate quarantine), and a minimum-exposure floor (controller will not revert until rollout has at least N samples to avoid noise-driven flips)
Traffic control: integrate with rollout-controller API to set traffic percentages atomically; support three actions: reduce by X%, pause, or full revert to previous model variant
Audit and explainability: store decision snapshots in object store and link to rollout event; include top contributing probe examples and delta histograms
Backfills: provide a backfill mode to re-evaluate historical rollout traces for parameter tuning and calculating false-revert statistics
rollout_strategy: Default staged A/B workflow: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with controller monitoring at each step
Controller waits a minimum sample count and minimum time at each step before allowing automatic promotion to next step
If controller triggers revert: immediate step back to last stable fraction, mark rollout as 'quarantined', and create an incident ticket with provenance
For low-risk feature flags, support automated low-latency roll-forward if posterior shows improvement beyond configured margin
monitoring_and_eval: Primary probe set: 250 instruction-following examples stratified by length, domain, and format
Secondary probes: safety heuristics (toxic language detection), latency probes, and economic metrics (tokens per request cost delta)
Per-cohort telemetry: track metrics by customer tier, region, and route so controller can surface targeted regressions
Dashboards: rollout detail view with live metric sparkline, posterior probability timeline, and top contributing probes
Alerting: integrated with PagerDuty for high-severity quarantines and with Slack for warnings when marginal regressions trend towards threshold
automation_policy: Default policy: automated revert permitted for open-source and internal customers; enterprise customers can opt into automated reversion via a contract flag
Cooldown: after automated revert, the controller enforces a 60-minute cooldown on that rollout to allow human investigation
Manual overrides: system exposes a 'force continue' that requires a human reviewer and an audit reason
Graceful degrade: if controller cannot reach metric backend, it will default to conservative behavior (pause promotion but not revert) to avoid acting on stale data
progress_updates: 2026-01-20: Spike complete — evaluated Bayesian seq-test vs SPRT on 12 of last rollouts; Bayesian approach had ~15% fewer false alarms while keeping detection latency comparable
2026-02-05: Implemented probe runner and can run synthetic probes against staging instances; baseline instrumentation in rollout-controller merged (see PR #641)
2026-02-22: Tuned priors using 9 months of rollout traces; initial thresholds proposed by ML lead and passed design review
2026-03-03: Console audit view prototype reviewed by PM and Compliance; added extra provenance fields per feedback
2026-03-10: End-to-end test harness for simulated traffic created; initial false-revert on adversarial noise identified and mitigated with minimum-sample gating
risks: Noisy probes could still trigger premature reverts affecting business throughput — mitigated via minimum-sample gating and multi-metric veto
Incorrect priors cause slow detection or too many false positives — mitigate with backfill tuning and periodic re-calibration
Controller action latency during high load — ensure decision engine is horizontally scalable and does not block rollout-controller path
Enterprise customers may require non-automated mode by default: must keep clear opt-out model and contract-safe guards
testing_plan: Unit tests for metric aggregators and Bayesian engine with synthetic datasets
Integration tests that simulate staged rollouts using historical traces and assert revert/no-revert decisions match golden labels
Chaos test: introduce bursty noise and verify minimum-sample and veto logic prevent flapping
Canary in staging: run controller enabled on internal-only rollouts for two weeks before enabling automated reverts in prod
Periodic adversarial evaluation: run a daily adversarial probe generator to estimate worst-case false-positive risk
